scope: Standalone localhost synthetic transport comparison. No ScanForge code, public MCP session, application files, or real project data were used.
method: In separate guarded Chrome processes, construct and transmit 1400 changing JSON messages through either HTTP POST with Blob bodies or one WebSocket with text messages and per-message acknowledgments. A disposable Node server consumes each payload and verifies its combined SHA-256 against independently generated expected messages. Both sent 489346490 bytes with SHA-256 47dfc4f73dd3496233536c0ba6c0644200c4c4f7300ac55f7438aa79e2484bd0.
fullWebsocketControl: The WebSocket probe also transferred 1835 changing messages and verified the combined digest 1344960f3bce6403149f180b24b2454f3537ef50068d741f0e44bad3d156eccf at a 583413760-byte guarded peak. This used the previous source revision without the later optional-count argument; the matching 1400-message comparison uses the retained source.
httpLongerFailure: A separate 1835-message HTTP attempt failed at request 1499 after 523950356 bytes with TypeError: Failed to fetch; the server-side cause is not established. Its guarded peak was 1709273088 bytes; cleanup confirmed. This standalone failure is not evidence that ScanForge MCP fails at that count.
interpretation: The synthetic text WebSocket used less total Job memory in this matched single-run comparison, at a small elapsed-time cost. The protocols, server processing, and browser memory allocation differ; this does not prove the reduction survives real artifact creation, bridge authorization, GUI reopen, or mixed traffic.
securityAndCorrectness: The disposable probe has no authentication, origin checks, session ownership, bounded production frame parser, reconnection, timeouts, retry semantics, cancellation or compatibility negotiation. It must not be used as a production bridge. A production candidate would require these contracts, a maintained protocol implementation, end-to-end byte validation, failure tests, and guarded real-project replay before consideration.
cleanup: All guarded processes terminated. The temporary checkout copy was verified against the retained diagnostic and removed. The separately launched empty QuickSurface instance was closed after activation failed twice; no native project or user application was changed.
limitations: Single samples, no instrumented breakdown, and matching same-origin localhost rather than the application's cross-origin HTTP bridge. Neither M2 nor its 4 GiB large-project gate is complete.
